purpose: Maps an annotated VCF's INFO fields onto evidence fields for acmg_pipeline.providers.vcf_annotation. Which field means what is a property of the annotator that wrote the file, so this MUST be checked against a real header from the annotator actually in use before it is applied. Nothing here has been validated against an operational file.
limitations: The VEP entry is derived from VEP's documented CSQ layout, not from an output file this project has seen. VEP's field set depends on which plugins and --fields were used, so the subfield names present in a real header may differ.

The bcftools entry assumes gnomAD-prefixed field names from `bcftools annotate -a gnomad.vcf.gz -c INFO/gnomAD_AF,...`. The names are whatever the -c argument assigned, so they are installation-specific.
Both are starting points for reading a real header, not defaults to apply unseen.
Fields a curator already concluded (CLNSIG, ACMG_CODES and the rest of providers.vcf_annotation.REFUSED) cannot appear here; the provider raises if they do.

ensembl-vep-vcf.note: `vep --vcf` packs every subfield into CSQ and declares the order in the ##INFO header's Format clause. The provider reads that clause, so the order below is not relied on - only the names are. One entry per transcript is present; only the entry matching the transcript being evaluated is read.

snpeff-vcf.note: SnpEff's ANN field has the same shape with different subfield names, declared as "Functional annotations: 'Allele | Annotation | ...'". Included to show the second shape the provider handles; the field list is illustrative.

bcftools-annotate-gnomad.note: Flat one-field-per-value output. Fields sharing a `group` become one evidence record, so AF, AC and AN arrive together as a single population observation. `callable` is not derivable from these fields and is deliberately absent - usable_observations() requires it for an AC of 0, so an absent variant still cannot be read as AF 0.
